Focus component: model_design. Use Tier 2 architectural deepening: introduce parallel local and dilated temporal filtering within the existing NextItNet blocks. The content-dependent gating attempt tied validation HR@10 at 0.625, so the next experiment should change which temporal patterns the model extracts. A plausible limitation is that higher-dilation blocks sample widely spaced interactions without directly accessing adjacent transitions in their first temporal filter; this is a hypothesis, not an established cause of the plateau.

In each block with dilation greater than one, add a parallel depthwise convolution with dilation 1 and the same kernel size as conv1. Apply the existing normalized, masked input to both branches, left-pad each according to its dilation, and average their outputs before the existing mix1 projection. Keep dilation-1 blocks, conv2, mix2, activations, residual connections, normalization, dropout, embeddings, and candidate scoring unchanged. This single modification lets higher-dilation blocks learn immediate item transitions alongside longer-range patterns while preserving strictly causal computation and one NextItNet model.

Start from the supplied ungated depthwise model and retain all eight constants, constructor and method interfaces, permitted imports, and the two-class source structure. Allocate one candidate slot to this change and let the frozen host train and compare validation HR@10 against 0.625 using its unchanged protocol. Treat a gain as evidence for multiscale temporal filtering, while recognizing that selection on 200 validation users provides limited evidence of generalization.
